sequence.description: The log's head once the command committed: its last event, or the head it saw when it appended none.

changed.description: False for a command that was accepted and changed nothing, so appended no event.

sequence.description: The log's head when the command was rejected.

reason.description: Why the command was rejected, the code of its error: not_found when its target does not exist.

code.description: A stable error code in snake case.

error.description: The rejection as an error: its code (the reason), a message for people and structured data.

receipt.description: A command's receipt: accepted (with the head sequence after it and whether it changed anything) or rejected (with the reason and the error). A retry with the same commandId answers the same receipt.

result.description: The method's result, present when this request applied the command; absent on a retry and on a rejection.

section.description: A section of the denylist: browserDomains (where a browser verb may not go unasked), paths (files and directories), commandPatterns (shell command lines), or hosts (what a command, a fetch, a search or one of the harness's own tools may not reach unasked).

id.description: The entry's id, unique in its section: a preset's is the same on every environment.

pattern.description: The pattern, in its section's grammar.

note.description: Why the entry is there, for people; empty for none.

preset.description: Whether it came from the presets (seeded on first start, or restored); an edited preset keeps it.

enabled.description: Whether it matches: a disabled entry never does.

entry.description: One entry of the denylist: its id, pattern, note, whether it is a preset, and whether it is enabled.

restored.description: The presets put back, by section, in the order they were added.

id.description: The entry's id, unique in its section: a preset's is the same on every environment.

pattern.description: A host name, IPv4 address or IPv6 literal, with an optional leading wildcard label (*.example.com): no scheme, port or path.

note.description: Why the entry is there, for people; empty for none.

preset.description: Whether it came from the presets (seeded on first start, or restored); an edited preset keeps it.

enabled.description: Whether it matches: a disabled entry never does.

browserDomains.description: Where a browser verb may not go unasked, by domain.

id.description: The entry's id, unique in its section: a preset's is the same on every environment.

pattern.description: An absolute or ~-relative path, with glob segments: * and ? within a segment, ** for any number of segments.

note.description: Why the entry is there, for people; empty for none.

preset.description: Whether it came from the presets (seeded on first start, or restored); an edited preset keeps it.

enabled.description: Whether it matches: a disabled entry never does.

paths.description: Files and directories, and everything under a directory.

id.description: The entry's id, unique in its section: a preset's is the same on every environment.

pattern.description: Tokens separated by white space: a bare * matches any run of tokens including none, a * inside a token anything within that token.

note.description: Why the entry is there, for people; empty for none.

preset.description: Whether it came from the presets (seeded on first start, or restored); an edited preset keeps it.

enabled.description: Whether it matches: a disabled entry never does.

id.description: The entry's id, unique in its section: a preset's is the same on every environment.

pattern.description: A host name, IPv4 address or IPv6 literal, with an optional leading wildcard label (*.example.com): no scheme, port or path.

note.description: Why the entry is there, for people; empty for none.

preset.description: Whether it came from the presets (seeded on first start, or restored); an edited preset keeps it.

enabled.description: Whether it matches: a disabled entry never does.

hosts.description: Hosts a command, a fetch, a search or one of the harness's own tools may not reach unasked.

denylist.description: The environment's denylist: its four sections, each an ordered list of entries in the section's grammar.
